Module 1 · Definition
Middleware is the software in the middle that receives requests, hosts the application’s code and connects systems safely.
User
Middleware
Data
Middleware is a category. Apache, Tomcat and Kafka are products in it. It can run as its own server, inside an app, or as a cloud service.
Module 1 · What is middleware?
Eight jobs middleware does, so apps don’t have to
Communication
connect apps over the network
Routing
send each request to the right app
Security
who may come in, encryption
Load balancing
share traffic across servers
Messaging
pass messages without waiting
Hosting
a place for app code to run
Monitoring
logs and numbers for troubleshooting
Reliability
retries, failover, keep running
No single product does all eight. Each family covers some of them.

Module 1 · One new word
What is an API? A door made for programs
Website · for people
My Bank
Savings · 1234
₹42,500
Transfer
The server sends the whole page: text, colours, buttons. Ready to look at.
API · for programs
{ "account": "1234", "balance": 42500 }
The server sends only the data. The phone app draws its own screen with it.
Your phone is calling APIs all day:
UPI app asks
“What’s my balance?” → ₹42,500
Weather app asks
“How hot is it now?” → 31 °C
Cab app asks
“Where is my driver?” → 2 min away
An API is an address a program calls with a question or a task. No screen. Just the answer.
Module 1 · APIs

MY BANK · MENU
Show my balance

Send money
/api/transfers

/api/accounts/1234/history
You order only what is on the menu.
You order by name. Each dish has an address.
You never see the kitchen.
Module 1 · APIs
One API, many apps, so it needs a guard
Phone app
Website
Partner bank
An attacker
API gateway
checks every caller
Bank’s APIs
balance · transfers · history
Build the API once, every app uses it. But anyone on the internet can knock, so a guard stands at the door.
Module 1 · A real example
You check your bank balance: six steps
1 · Phone asks
the app sends a web request
2 · API gateway
checks who you are, if you’re allowed, and how often you call
3 · Web server (sometimes)
passes it to the right app server
4 · App server
runs the bank’s code (e.g. in Tomcat)
5 · Database
returns your balance
6 · Back to you
the answer travels back the same way
Blue boxes are middleware. The bank’s code is the application; Tomcat is what hosts it. Dashed = not every company has it, and some put it first. Each box is one hop.

Module 2 · Linux basics · Moving around
ls: what is in this folder?
ls
Names only
ls -l
Long list: one line per file, with details
ls -a
All: also hidden files (name starts with a dot)
ls -lh
Human sizes: 1.2K, 4.5M, 2.0G
ls -lt
Newest first, handy for log folders
ls -lah /etc
Join options. List any folder without going there.
$ ls backup notes $ ls -a # hidden files appear . .. .bashrc .profile backup notes $ ls -lh drwxrwxr-x 2 trainee01 trainee01 4.0K Nov 11 10:05 backup drwxrwxr-x 2 trainee01 trainee01 4.0K Nov 11 10:02 notes
-l -a -h and -lah mean the same thing. Order does not matter.

free or available? Think of a restaurant

eating
eating
eating
eating
eating
snacks

snacks

snacks

snacks
clear in 1 sec
empty
free = 1 table

used · busy with programs

Module 2 · Linux basics · Network
Refused and timed out are different problems
nc knocks on a door. Three things can happen:
succeeded
The door opens.
$ nc -vz localhost 22
… succeeded!
ANSWER COMES
instantly
All good: a service is listening.
refused
You knock. A voice says “nobody here”.
$ nc -vz localhost 9999
… Connection refused
ANSWER COMES
instantly
Service problem: start it, or check the port number.
timed out
You knock… silence. You wait and give up.
$ nc -vz -w 5 10.255.255.1 22
… timed out
ANSWER COMES
after 5 seconds
Network problem: firewall or route. Call the network team.
Fast “no” = look at the service. Slow silence = look at the network.

HTTP forgets you. Cookies remember.
Every request stands alone: the server has no memory of the last one. A cookie fixes that.
1 · Browser: POST /login (name + password)
2 · Server: 200 OK + Set-Cookie: session=7f3a9
3 · Browser: GET /balance + Cookie: session=7f3a9
4 · Server: “Ah, it’s trainee01” → your balance
Like a cloakroom token: show it every time and you get your coat back.

<Directory /> Require all denied </Directory> <Directory /var/www/> Require all granted </Directory>
Default “no” for the whole disk, then “yes” only where websites live. Safe by design.

The block that opens /var/www
① <Directory /var/www/> ② Options Indexes FollowSymLinks ③ AllowOverride None ④ Require all granted </Directory>
① Directory
this folder and every folder below it
② Options
extra features: Indexes = folder listing, FollowSymLinks = follow shortcuts
③ AllowOverride
None = ignore .htaccess files in folders
④ Require
who may read: here, everyone
Only ④ decides yes or no. The next slide shows its choices.

Module 3 · Apache · Folder access
A site in a new folder gets 403. Here is why.
1 · The site file says
DocumentRoot /srv/shop
2 · The visitor gets
403 Forbidden
3 · Because
/srv is still locked by <Directory />
error.log
[authz_core:error] [client 127.0.0.1] AH01630: client denied by server configuration: /srv/shop/
Fix: open just that folder, next to the site
<Directory /srv/shop> Require all granted </Directory>
Then configtest → reload → curl. Open the one folder you need, never <Directory />.

Module 3 · Apache
Lock a folder, read the log, unlock it
$ sudo mkdir /var/www/html/private $ echo "secret" | sudo tee /var/www/html/private/index.html $ sudo vi /etc/apache2/sites-available/000-default.conf # inside <VirtualHost> add: <Directory /var/www/html/private> Require all denied </Directory> $ sudo apache2ctl configtest && sudo systemctl reload apache2 $ curl -I localhost/private/ # 403 $ sudo tail -n 2 /var/log/apache2/error.log # AH01630
Now change denied to local, reload, and curl again. What changes, and why?

├── .htaccess ← read first

→

Redirect /blog/old.html /blog/new.html ErrorDocument 404 /blog/404.html
Apache reads this file on every request to that folder.
AllowOverride None
.htaccess is ignored (Ubuntu default)
AllowOverride All
.htaccess is read and obeyed
Some web apps ship one and need All. Otherwise keep None: faster, and all rules stay in /etc.

Parent Directory

db-dump.sql

Options Indexes + no index.html = a list of every file. Anyone can download them.
Turn it off in the <Directory> block:

Module 3 · Apache · Pages
Who should own the website files?
Do
$ ls -l /var/www/portal -rw-r--r-- root root index.html $ ls -ld /var/www/portal drwxr-xr-x root root portal
Folders 755, files 644. www-data only needs to read.
Don’t
chmod 777
anyone can change your site
chown www-data
a tricked worker can rewrite every page
Both “fix” a 403 and open a security hole.

Module 3 · Apache · Safe changes
Reload or restart?
reload
Re-reads the settings. Visitors are not cut off.
Use for site and config changes.
restart
Stops, then starts. Active visitors are dropped.
Needed for some bigger changes.

On by default, but only from the server itself: Require local.
Busy close to the maximum and pages slow? The waiters are all taken. More on Day 2 (performance).
Module 3 · Apache · Capacity
How many visitors at once? MaxRequestWorkers
Ubuntu default: event MPM. Each child process holds 25 threads (waiters).
child process 1
25 threads
child process 2
25 threads
At start: 2 × 25 = 50 waiters. That is the 1 busy + 49 idle in server-status.
Grows when busy, up to the limit:
50
150
MaxRequestWorkers 150
All 150 busy? New visitors wait in a queue. Pages feel slow, then time out.
Settings live in mods-enabled/mpm_event.conf. Tuning them is Day 2 (performance).

KeepAlive: one connection, many requests
One browser, one connection, over time →
connect
page
style.css
logo.png
idle 5 s
closed
KeepAlive On
reuse the connection: faster pages
KeepAliveTimeout 5
idle for 5 s? close it, free the waiter
Timeout 300
give up on a stuck request after 300 s

Module 3 · Apache · Logs
Old logs are rotated, not lost
$ ls /var/log/apache2
access.log
today, still being written
access.log.1
yesterday
access.log.2.gz
2 days ago, compressed
…
access.log.14.gz
the oldest kept, then deleted
Every night, logrotate renames today’s log to .1, compresses older ones to .gz, and keeps 14 days.
Read a compressed log without unpacking:
$ zcat access.log.2.gz | grep " 404 " $ zgrep -c " 404 " access.log.*.gz
“It happened last Tuesday” → look in .1 or .N.gz, not only in access.log.

One waiter per table, or one fast waiter
Classic Apache

Module 4 · Nginx · Processes
Nginx is a team too: one master, a few workers
$ ps -ef | grep nginx root 2101 1 nginx: master process /usr/sbin/nginx www-data 2102 2101 nginx: worker process www-data 2103 2101 nginx: worker process
master · root
opens the ports, reads the config, manages workers
worker · www-data
serves visitors: thousands each
Same idea as Apache. The difference: one worker per CPU core, each juggling many visitors.
Module 4 · Nginx · Install
Install Nginx… and it fails to start
$ sudo apt install -y nginx Job for nginx.service failed… $ journalctl -u nginx -n 5 bind() to 0.0.0.0:80 failed (98: Address already in use)
Nginx also wants port 80, but Apache already has it.
We will give Nginx port 8081 instead.
Module 4 · Nginx · Why it failed
Why Nginx wanted port 80: its default site
/etc/nginx/sites-available/default
server { listen 80 default_server; root /var/www/html; index index.html index.nginx-debian.html; server_name _; }
Installing Nginx also switched on this site, which asks for port 80. Apache already had it.
The fix in the Try-it: remove its link from sites-enabled, then give our shop site port 8081.

Module 4 · Nginx · Config
location: different rules for different paths
server { location / { … } # everything else location /images/ { … } # starts with /images/ location = /health { … } # exactly /health }
location /path
paths that start with it
location = /path
only exactly this path
Several match? The longest one wins. = beats everything.
Like Apache’s <Directory>, but for URL paths instead of folders.
Module 4 · Nginx · Config
try_files, one step at a time
location / { try_files $uri $uri/ =404; }
A visitor asks for /sale.html:
$uri
is there a file /var/www/shop/sale.html? Yes → send it
→
$uri/
no? is there a folder with an index file? Yes → send that
→
=404
neither? answer 404 Not Found
Module 4 · Nginx · Config
root adds the path. alias replaces it.
A visitor asks for /images/logo.png
root
location /images/ { root /data; }
Nginx looks for:
/data
/images/logo.png
root + the whole URL path
alias
location /images/ { alias /data/pics/; }
Nginx looks for:
/data/pics/
logo.png
/images/ is swapped for the alias
Wrong one = 404, and error.log shows the path Nginx really tried.

Module 4 · Nginx · Common failures
Three Nginx errors you will meet
Missing ; (found by nginx -t)
[emerg] directive "root" is not terminated by ";" in …/shop:5
Add the ; on the line it names, test again.
403: no index file
directory index of "/var/www/shop/images/" is forbidden
Add an index.html, or autoindex on if a listing is really wanted.
403: Linux permissions
open() "/var/www/shop/index.html" failed (13: Permission denied)
www-data cannot read it: chmod 644 file, 755 folders (Module 2).
Module 4 · Nginx · Common failures
nginx -t passed, but read the warnings
sites-enabled/shop
server_name shop.example.com;
sites-enabled/shop-copy
server_name shop.example.com;
→
$ sudo nginx -t nginx: [warn] conflicting server name "shop.example.com" on 0.0.0.0:8081, ignored nginx: configuration file … test is successful
The second block is silently ignored. Your change in it never takes effect.
“test is successful” means it will load, not that it does what you meant. Read every [warn] line.
Try it · 6 min

Status codes, one at a time, on all three servers
2xx
it worked
3xx
go somewhere else

the request is the problem

Already met: 200 · 404 · 403 · 301 · 401 · 500. Next slides: 206 · 302 · 304 · 307/308 · 400 · 405 · 408 · 413 · 414.

Module 4 · Status codes in depth
206 Partial Content
206
Partial Content
“Here is only the part you asked for.” Downloads that resume, videos that skip ahead.
Make it happen
$ curl -i -r 0-4 localhost/hello.html HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content Content-Range: bytes 0-4/21 Hello
In the log
"GET /hello.html HTTP/1.1" 206 5
Apache
on by default for static files
Nginx
on by default
IIS
on by default
Many 206s for one big file = someone streaming or resuming a download. Not an error.
Module 4 · Status codes in depth
Four redirects: 301, 302, 307, 308
CODE
MEANS
BROWSER REMEMBERS IT?
A POST STAYS A POST?
301
moved for good
yes, cached for a long time
may turn into GET
302
moved for now
no
may turn into GET
307
moved for now
no
yes, kept
308
moved for good
yes
yes, kept
Apache: Redirect temp /sale.html /hello.html # 302 Nginx: return 302 /hello.html; IIS: HTTP Redirect → Status code: Found (302)
Module 4 · Status codes in depth
304 Not Modified
304
Not Modified
“You already have the latest copy. Use yours.” No body is sent: faster, less traffic.
Make it happen
$ curl -I localhost/hello.html | grep Last-Modified Last-Modified: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 04:15:00 GMT $ curl -I -H "If-Modified-Since: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 04:15:00 GMT" \ localhost/hello.html HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
In the log
"GET /hello.html HTTP/1.1" 304 180
Apache
on by default (Last-Modified, ETag)
Nginx
on by default
IIS
on by default
Changed a page but users still see the old one? Their copy is fresh in cache: check Last-Modified and Cache-Control.
Module 4 · Status codes in depth
400 Bad Request
400
Bad Request
“I can’t understand what you sent.” Broken or incomplete request.
Make it happen
$ printf 'GET / HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n' | nc localhost 80 # no Host header HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Apache error.log
AH00569: client sent HTTP/1.1 request without hostname
Apache
HTTP/1.1 without Host → 400
Nginx
same → 400
IIS
Bad Request – Invalid Hostname: no binding matches
IIS special: “Invalid Hostname” means the Host header matches no site binding. Check the bindings first.
Module 4 · Status codes in depth
405 Method Not Allowed
405
Method Not Allowed
“This address exists, but not for that method.” A static file cannot accept a POST or DELETE.
Make it happen
$ curl -i -X POST localhost:8081/ HTTP/1.1 405 Not Allowed $ curl -I -X DELETE localhost/hello.html # Apache HTTP/1.1 405 Method Not Allowed
In the log
"POST / HTTP/1.1" 405 166
Apache
DELETE on a static file → 405
Nginx
POST on a static file → 405
IIS
405.0: verb not allowed for the handler
A form or API call that works on one server and gets 405 on another: the request reached a static server, not the application.
Module 4 · Status codes in depth
408 Request Timeout
408
Request Timeout
“You connected, then said nothing for too long.” The server closes the connection.
Make it happen
$ nc localhost 80 # connect, type nothing # … about 20 seconds later Apache gives up
In the log
127.0.0.1 - - [11/Nov/2026:10:31:02 +0530] "-" 408 0
Apache
mod_reqtimeout: header 20–40 s
Nginx
client_header_timeout 60s
IIS
HTTP.sys ConnectionTimeout 120 s
Lots of "-" 408 lines? Usually browsers opening spare connections they never used. Harmless.
Module 4 · Status codes in depth
413 Payload Too Large
413
Payload Too Large
“What you are sending is bigger than I accept.” Usually a file upload.
Make it happen
$ head -c 2000000 /dev/zero > big.bin # a 2 MB file $ curl -i -X POST --data-binary @big.bin localhost:8081/ HTTP/1.1 413 Request Entity Too Large
Nginx error.log
client intended to send too large body: 2000000 bytes
Apache
LimitRequestBody (1 GB)
Nginx
client_max_body_size 1m
IIS
maxAllowedContentLength 30 MB → 404.13
“Upload fails over 1 MB” on Nginx is client_max_body_size, almost every time.
Module 4 · Status codes in depth
414 URI Too Long
414
URI Too Long
“Your address is longer than I accept.” Often a broken link or a huge search string.
Make it happen
$ curl -I "localhost/$(printf 'a%.0s' {1..9000})" # 9,000 letters HTTP/1.1 414 Request-URI Too Long
In the log
"GET /aaaaaaaa…" 414
Apache
LimitRequestLine 8190
Nginx
large_client_header_buffers 4 8k
IIS
maxUrl 4096 → 404.14
Users of one app hit 414 after it adds more to the URL? The app should use POST, not a bigger limit.
Try it · 8 min

$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" localhost/hello.html # 200 $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -r 0-4 localhost/hello.html # 206 $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" localhost/old.html # 301 $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" localhost/nothing.html # 404 $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" localhost/private/ # 403 $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" localhost/admin/ # 401 $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST localhost:8081/ # 405 $ sudo cut -d' ' -f9 /var/log/apache2/access.log | sort | uniq -c

Module 5 · Tomcat · Install · Step 1
First, a user just for Tomcat
$ sudo useradd -r -m -U \ -d /opt/tomcat \ -s /bin/false tomcat
-r a system user
-d /opt/tomcat its home folder
-s /bin/false nobody can log in as it
Why? If the app is attacked, the attacker gets a weak user, not root.

Module 7 · Load balancing
In Nginx: one upstream list, one proxy_pass
upstream payment_app { server 10.0.0.31:8080; server 10.0.0.32:8080; server 10.0.0.33:8080; } server { listen 8081; location /payment/ { proxy_pass http://payment_app; } }
upstream = the list of copies
proxy_pass points at the list, not one server
Default: take turns (“round robin”)

The server side failed

5
Nginx: 502. Apache: usually 503. Read each error log.
6
curl Tomcat directly. If that fails too, it is Tomcat’s problem.
7
Only the 500. Kong made the others itself.
8
Timed out. Refused means nothing is listening.

Module 2 · Linux basics
Catch your own login in the log
Terminal 1
$ sudo tail -f /var/log/auth.log
Terminal 2 (new window)
$ ssh [user]@[vm-ip] # type a wrong password once # then the right one
Then: sudo grep -c "Failed password" /var/log/auth.log · journalctl -u ssh -n 10
